newsitem.title: USA: Newsweek reports suspects in Colorado child murder.
newsitem.headline: Newsweek reports suspects in Colorado child murder.

text.p: The three-week investigation into the murder of child beauty queen JonBenet Ramsey continued on Sunday, with no named suspects, according to a spokesman for the Boulder, Colo., police.
However, police have identified suspects in the strangling of the six-year-old beauty pagent winner, according to Newsweek magazine's Jan. 20 issue, released on Sunday.

"A source close to the Ramsey family tells Newsweek that handwriting analysis experts hired by the family's attorneys have examined the ransom note and concluded the original note was not written by anyone in the immediate family," the magazine said.

"Police are still processing the handwriting, blood and hair samples taken not only from the Ramseys and their family members, but also employees and friends who had been in their Boulder, Colorado home at or before the time of the murder..." the magazine reported.
"Newsweek has learned that the number of suspects in the murder case has been narrowed to possibly as few as seven or eight."
The child's body was found Dec. 26 by her father in the basement of the family's 15-room home some eight hours after her mother said she found a ransom note demanding $118,000.
Published reports said there appeared to be no forced entry into the home and local authorities played down remarks by the mother, Patricia Ramsey, that there was a "killer on the loose" in Boulder.

Another mystery surfaced over the weekend when it was revealed that the supermarket tabloid the Globe had obtained autopsy and crime scene photos, prompting the anguished parents to call the publishers of the tabloid "jackals, not journalists."
Boulder County Coroner John Meyer asked Sheriff George Epp to conduct a probe into how official coroner's photos could have been leaked to the Florida-based Globe.
Deputies worked through the weekend, interviewing people inside and outside the coroner's office. An outside firm processes film for the coroner, but officials declined to identify the company.

Local supermarket chains said they would not sell the issue -- due to be on newsstands in the Denver area on Monday -- because the police fear publication of the photos could jeopardise the investigation.

The parents have hired a Washington-based media specialist and have yet to sit down with the police for a formal interview. They have also hired a private investigator to ferret out details of the case.
John Ramsey is a prominent business executive, who heads Access Graphics; his wife is a former Miss West Virginia.
